about: Real-word OCR / source errors that the generic garble detector cannot see (the misread is itself an English word). Every sentence matching a pattern is rejected (never repaired: the repair would not be a pure character fix or would be a guess). Sources: audit issues.csv rows (issue_row) and the STEP 2 review. v4 (STEP 2, 2026-11-03): adds 'fix_rules' = reviewed line-level OCR repairs (applied by scripts/s02_sentences.py to the raw words of that clawwords.md line only; the sentence gets ocr_fixed=1, sentence_raw keeps the original, every use is logged in ocr_fixes.csv). A fix is listed only when the misread is unambiguous (single word, the correct form is attested in the same text or is a fixed collocation); otherwise a reject pattern is used and another sentence is chosen. v4.1 (2026-11-04 re-audit must-fix): 'pattern_fix_rules' P1-P5 = context-guarded general OCR repairs applied by scripts/s02_sentences.py (textfix.pattern_fixes) to every rendered body sentence (ocr_fixed=1, logged in ocr_fixes.csv as pattern_fix:Pn); fix_rules F9/F10 = 'it' read for 'if'.

scan_about: v4 real-word scan (scripts/s06_ocr_scan.py) over every selected sentence: each candidate was read; confirmed misreads are reject_patterns (source 'v4 real-word OCR scan') or fix_rules; every other candidate is listed in scan_reviewed_not_errors (sentence_id, word, suggested variant).

pattern_fix_rules.guard: capital I + lowercase d, standalone, followed by a lowercase word (excludes 'ID', 'id', 'Id.')
pattern_fix_rules.why: OCR dropped the apostrophe of I'd

pattern_fix_rules.guard: standalone 'Ill' (not 'Ill-'), followed by a lowercase word; NOT after a capitalised word without punctuation (regnal numeral III: 'King George Ill', 'Napoleon Ill'); NOT when 'ill <next word>' (the adjective, e.g. 'ill health') is attested in clawwords.md
pattern_fix_rules.why: OCR dropped the apostrophe of I'll
OCR dropped the apostrophe of you'll

pattern_fix_rules.guard: capital 'There' at the start of the sentence (or after a quote mark / sentence end), so 'will there be', 'could there be' are never touched
pattern_fix_rules.why: OCR lost "'ll" (ungrammatical 'There be'); the next sentence of the same turn has "there'll be" (L72621)
